I can believe it for the below section, but not for this bit running in a goroutine.

1. Imagine 3 successive calls A, B, C resulting in a run of this goroutine.
2. Call A happens first, takes the lock, and then the CPU context-switches away.
3. Then call B starts and blocks waiting for the lock

How does this prevent out of order execution? The prior code arguably might have been serialized but this code could end up with e.g. two copies of this goroutine both waiting on the lock, then the "wrong" one gets it first.

Can you actually move this up one line, before the Done()? I think as soon as Get() has returned something it should no longer be considered queued (otherwise a caller checking IsQueued may fail to add something to the queue even though they should).
